source_title: Open-source image editor focused on PSD compatibility and workflows familiar to Adobe Photoshop users. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
A free, open-source image editor for Windows, macOS, Linux, and the browser. Built with a focus on accurate PSD compatibility, keeping text, vectors, masks, layer styles, and Smart Objects editable when working with layered Photoshop files. Work in limited palettes without flattening your layers, bring in Affinity, Krita, GIMP, OpenRaster, Paint.NET, and PDF artwork, and extend the editor with classic plug-ins and JavaScript.
Download · Try in your browser · Features · Full gallery
For bug reports and feature requests, please open an issue or post in Discussions . These are the best places to post because search engines can index them, helping others find the questions and answers. Want to chat? Join Seth's Discord .
Designed to feel familiar if you're used to Photoshop's workflows and keyboard shortcuts.
Latest release: 1.24 · November 1, 2026 · Release notes · All releases
Windows releases are code signed by Seth A. Robinson; the macOS app is signed and notarized (Robinson Technologies Corporation); the Linux Flatpak repository is GPG signed. Every release is published on the GitHub Releases page with SHA-256 checksums.
Paste this into a terminal. It installs Patchy for your user from the Patchy Flatpak repository and pulls the shared KDE runtime from Flathub. No root needed.
Patchy then updates with flatpak update or through your software center, and starts from your application menu or with flatpak run com.rtsoft.patchy .
This needs the flatpak tool. Fedora and openSUSE desktops usually have it already. If needed, install it first with sudo apt install flatpak (Ubuntu, Debian), sudo dnf install flatpak (Fedora) or sudo zypper install flatpak (openSUSE).
If you already use flatpak system-wide, you can use --system in place of --user . Patchy then reuses the runtime extensions you already have (graphics drivers, codecs) instead of downloading them again. Installing that way may ask for an admin password.
The .flatpakref link in the table downloads a small file that a Flatpak-aware software center (GNOME Software, KDE Discover) can open to install Patchy. Ubuntu has none by default, and on Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME Software's Open button fails to start Flatpak apps, so use the terminal command above instead.
The single-file bundle is the same build, for when you would rather download a file first. Install it with flatpak install --user PatchyLinux.flatpak . It still fetches the KDE runtime from Flathub, and it updates from the same repository afterwards.
My flatpak knowledge is limited, so I hope all this makes sense. I hope to submit Patchy to Flathub eventually, but for now we have our own repository.
PatchyLinux.AppImage is one file that runs without installing anything, on Ubuntu 22.04 or newer (or another distro from 2022 on: Debian 12, Fedora 36, Mint 21 and so on). It updates itself, so keep it somewhere you can write to, such as ~/Applications :
( curl -LO works instead of wget -O PatchyLinux.AppImage .) You can also make it executable from your file manager (Properties > Permissions, "Allow executing file as program") and double-click it.
The AppImage needs the FUSE 3 tools and libraries (not libfuse2 ), which most desktops already have. If it says it cannot mount itself, install it:
Without FUSE (some containers and minimal systems), run it with ./PatchyLinux.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run .
To add Patchy to your application menu, use an AppImage integration tool: Gear Lever (a Flatpak app: open the AppImage with it), AppImageLauncher (offers to integrate an AppImage the first time you open it), AM (command line: am --launcher ./PatchyLinux.AppImage ), or AppImage Manager .
When a new version is out, Patchy's update prompt can download it, replace the AppImage file and start again (if the file sits in a folder you can write to; otherwise it offers the download). AppImage tools such as Gear Lever or AppImageUpdate can also update it. For AI control, the connector command is the AppImage file with the argument patchy-mcp (Help > Set up AI Control shows the exact line). The AppImage opens HEIC images through your distribution's libheif (Ubuntu and Debian: the libheif1 package, plus libheif-plugin-libde265 on Ubuntu 24.04 and later); the Flatpak brings its own.
See it in action. Click an image for the full-size capture.
See the full gallery for painting, palette mode, seamless textures, Camera Raw, long shadows, scripting, and more.
Patchy's C++ foundation makes these integrations more straightforward: we can build on established C and C++ libraries such as G'MIC and implement classic Photoshop plug-in interfaces directly.
Full feature list and format support · Scripting guide · AI control setup
Local by design. No telemetry, tracking, or uploads of your images. The browser build runs the same editor locally through WebAssembly. Desktop builds have more memory available and add printing, scanner/camera import, and command-line automation. Optional update checks contact GitHub, as do the one-click updates (Windows and the Linux AppImage) and Object Selection's High Quality model, each downloaded only if you ask for it. Twelve interface languages, dark and light schemes, and importable themes are included.
The desktop and browser builds share the editor, with these differences:
Format support does not imply every source feature stays editable; see the format limits and current limitations . PDF import requires Qt PDF when building a custom desktop version. HEIC/HEIF availability depends on the installed decoder . The browser build also has tighter memory limits.
In the October 29, 2026 Testy v2 run , Patchy opened all 309 files of the psd-tools test collection, and Photoshop reopened every Patchy save with all 43 text objects, 183 adjustment layers, 172 Smart Objects, and 181 live effects kept. Patchy's perceptual render match was 98.7% , with 299 files within 10% of Photoshop's pixels, and its Photoshop text score was 97.3% , both the highest of the six programs tested against Photoshop's reference, using a Patchy 1.21 development build (commit 25822a64 ).
Testy v2 scores each program on what it draws itself: the baked pixels Photoshop stores for text, shapes, fills, and Smart Objects are removed first. That is stricter than the August run, so the two sets of numbers are not comparable.
These are dated, corpus-specific results. The linked report has every file's renders and difference maps for all seven columns. Read the full comparison and methodology for the tables, per-folder results, scoring rules, and limitations.
Know the limits: editing is RGB at 8, 16, or 32 bits per channel (the browser build stops at 16). CMYK work is proofing and export: CMYK Proof mode shows the print colors and saves CMYK JPEG, TIFF, and PDF, but pixels stay RGB. Lab and the other color modes convert to RGB on open, and there is no GPU acceleration. Unsupported Smart Filters can remain preview-locked, and Affinity import has format-specific limitations. See current compatibility .
Search Commands: Help > Search Commands (Ctrl+Shift+/) and a search button after the Help menu find any menu command, tool or keyboard command by its name, menu or a short description, and run it ( issue 554 )
Layer menu: commands sit in five groups with Fill and Merge submenus ( issue 546 ); Lock Layers... (Ctrl+/) opens a lock dialog ( issue 544 ); Hide Layers and Show Layers (Ctrl+,) and Show All Layers (Ctrl+Alt+,) ( issue 546 , issue 550 ); an Export submenu has Quick Export as PNG (Ctrl+Shift+') and Export As (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+') ( issue 545 )
Layers: Alt+[ and Alt+] select the layer below or above and wrap around the stack, Alt+Shift adds to the selection, also as Select > Layer Below and Layer Above ( issue 541 ); the eye tooltip names Alt-click for the other layers ( issue 549 ); the Layers footer can show a Merge Visible button and a Rasterize button whose menu also rasterizes the layer style ( issue 539 ); the Background layer's tooltip says Locked: Background ( issue 483 ); mask and saved channel thumbnails show 16 and 32-bit masks instead of white ( issue 540 )
Presets: comma and period step back and forward through the active tool's brush or gradient presets ( issue 543 )
32-bit color: in 32-bit documents the color windows and Color panel show linear values with an Intensity in stops, paint, fills, gradients and the Eyedropper keep values above 1.0, and gradient stops carry their own Intensity
Shapes: custom stroke dashes get an editable Dash pattern field and a Dash offset, Long and Short dashes, Sparse dots, Dash dot and Dash dot dot presets join Dashed and Dotted, and the presets set matching caps and corners ( issue 548 , issue 556 ); stroke presets can be saved, picked from the shape options bar and managed in Edit > Presets ( issue 557 ); the shape options bar has a dash list and an Appearance gear ( issue 556 ); the Shape Appearance dialog groups gradient and pattern settings under their rows ( issue 552 ); Inside and Outside strokes on open paths draw beside the line with their dashes spaced along it, as in Photoshop ( issue 553 , issue 558 )
Paths: Merge Shapes combines a layer's shapes into one outline, a point dragged onto its neighbor welds to it, Join closes open paths, Break Path at Point, Join End Points, Merge into One Point and Delete Segment edit points, selected shapes can be cut, copied, pasted, recolored, aligned or moved to a new layer, and Direct Select adds a point with a click on a segment ( issue 555 )
GIMP files: Patchy asks whether text layers GIMP painted over stay pixels, become editable text or get text copies, with a matching Preferences choice ( issue 551 ); GIMP 3.2 vector layers open as shape layers with their fill, stroke, caps, joins and dashes ( issue 548 ); the bottom layer opens unlocked ( issue 547 )
Text: the font list has a Recent section and Style and Language filters ( issue 569 , issue 570 )
Export for Web: presets, quality presets, a 2 x 2 compare view and a narrower settings column ( issue 571 )
Also: opening a file that is already open switches to its tab ( issue 560 ); the PSD compatibility report counts routine Photoshop blocks as understood and has a Don't show this again check ( issue 559 ); the opacity digit keys work from panels and the tool palette and 00 sets 0% ( issue 562 ); the Hotkeys page in Preferences keeps its search row in view ( issue 561 ); Gaussian blur is faster on large images ( issue 564 ); the Clone Stamp and Healing Brush hide the source overlay while Alt picks a new source ( issue 573 ); resize grips are visible in Light themes ( pull request 572 , thanks softwaregames1); number fields in the Flatpak show their values again on the KDE runtime's Qt 6.11.3; the tool cursor no longer shows over a window blocked by a dialog after Alt+Tab ( issue 504 )
Adjustments: Image > Adjustments > Black & White (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+B) has hue chips, a reading of how much of the image each slider acts on, a tint with Hue and Saturation, and 21 presets with thumbnails in Neutral and Tinted sections; Vibrance, Exposure, Channel Mixer, Photo Filter, Gradient Map, Selective Color and Color Lookup now apply directly from Image > Adjustments ( issue 528 )
Shapes and paths: 878 custom shapes from game-icons.net ship built in, loaded on first use, with arrows and signs in Arrows and Symbols and cards and dice in Games; polygons stay live, path components get W, H, X and Y fields and live rows, Combine Shapes has menus, and a click picks a work path among shapes ( issue 521 )
Edit > Fill opens a Fill dialog with Contents, Mode, Opacity and Preserve Transparency, on Shift+Backspace and Shift+F5 ( issue 530 )
Shortcuts: Shift+[ and Shift+] step brush hardness, the digit keys set layer opacity, / locks transparent pixels and Shift+Alt+letter sets the blend mode, on Photoshop's keys ( issue 522 , issue 527 , issue 529 , issue 531 )
Brushes: one center cross at every size, and Show Outline off shows that cross instead of the system crosshair ( issue 533 ); Show Overlay matches the painted pixels down to 1 px, drag strokes center on the pointer and a Soft Square tip paints square; the tip chooser gives names the whole cell in smaller text on up to two lines, with the full name in the tooltip, and seeded tips and patterns are no longer added twice on a fresh profile ( issue 506 ); Import Brushes opens in the folder it showed last ( issue 520 )
Move and layers: a Move drag inside a selection moves the selected pixels on their layer, with Auto-Select on or off ( issue 532 ); Ctrl over a layer or channel thumbnail shows add, subtract and intersect badges, and Channels rows combine selections with Shift and Alt ( issue 525 , issue 480 ); Merge Visible works on a single visible layer that has a mask, style, text, shape or other content to apply ( issue 519 )
Interface: the Layer Style dialog drags smaller than its tallest page and scrolls, and remembers its size ( issue 536 ); the Properties panel's divider drags it taller and its info rows wrap; combo boxes in Preferences and Customize Tool Palette are at least 90 px wide and Customize Tool Palette names its tab Layers Panel ( issue 526 , issue 537 , issue 538 ); leaving full screen keeps a maximized window maximized on Linux ( issue 491 ); the Filter Gallery list no longer scrolls sideways
Files: transparent flat images open as a plain transparent layer, and a Preferences option keeps the old layer mask ( issue 534 )
Choose Plugins > Open Plug-ins Folder , copy your .8bf files and their supporting files into it, then choose Plugins > Rescan Plug-in Folders . Both 32-bit and 64-bit filters appear under Plugins > Legacy Photoshop Plug-ins .
Filters run on the active pixel layer, respect the selection, and apply as one undoable step. A separate helper isolates plug-in crashes. Plug-ins still run with your user permissions, so install only ones you trust. KPT and other formerly full-screen filters get a bounded, movable window. Plug-in details .

This project was developed with significant assistance from AI tools. I mean, you can still blame me (Seth) for bugs, but I just wanted to mention it.
Note: All included textures/materials are real images taken by humans, not AI generated
AI has reached the point where you can use your favorite AI agent to add the missing feature you want.
Just give it the link to this repo and tell it "read AGENTS.md and add feature X to this project". It will read the code, read the tests, and add the feature.
I mean, that's kind the power of open source, amplified.
Whatever AI you use (the smarter the better), tell it (or more likely, it's reading this right now) to read AGENTS.md before doing anything else. It contains the build and repository-wide rules, then routes feature work to the relevant document under docs/ .
There are thousands of regression and benchmarking tests. AGENTS.md links agents to the testing guide that explains how to select and run them. Due to the size of some of the test files I use they aren't all included, it will skip tests that require missing files. I probably don't want any major features coming from outside, as there are wrong and right ways to do things, some of it a bit subjective. Remember, you can always go crazy in your own fork, have some fun! If you have a bug fix or feature you think fits this project's scope please open an issue or tweet/etc at me. If you want to submit a pull request, please look at the actual code and fully TEST IT YOURSELF before submitting, and if possible include screenshots of the actual changes so it's clear what you're doing. If you're using AI, use a good one (Fable/Astra+ class), we don't want barely working slop.
Don't trust AI to create and submit PRs with no oversight, I'll delete ones that have too much AI smell. Smell human. This is starting to sound weird but you know what I mean.
Independent development and compatibility
Patchy is an independently developed image editor. Our goal is to build something powerful, fast, free of unnecessary bloat, and ultimately a tool that fits what I'm doing, especially for game-dev use cases. Recreating Photoshop feature for feature is not the goal.
Our PSD compatibility work uses publicly available format documentation and observations of files and rendered output produced by a licensed copy of Photoshop. We have not decompiled or disassembled Photoshop. Patchy also implements the legacy 8BF plug-in interface for interoperability, using its own declarations without copying Adobe SDK code. This compatibility work helps people keep their documents editable and use existing plug-ins across applications.
We also take patents seriously. Some features are deliberately limited or omitted because of patent concerns. For example, Quick Select calculates the selection when you finish a stroke instead of updating it continuously as you paint. Our development constraints document these boundaries, which we revisit as relevant patents expire or our research changes.
